clue.text: Dick's familiar words sadly name every last dreamy town, very neglected

definitions.note: a dick is slang for a detective; this is the catchphrase popularly attached to Sherlock Holmes

indicators.note: sadly suggests the words are in a sorry state, so their letters are jumbled
neglected says the very-letter is left out of the jumble

explanation.surface: A melancholy description of a sleepy, run-down town where nothing is looked after.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder NAME EVERY LAST DREAMY TOWN has one letter too many: 'very neglected' says drop V, and the remaining letters rearrange ('sadly') into the phrase. Dick is old slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase is widely attributed to the detective Sherlock Holmes, addressing his companion, though never quite in that form in Conan Doyle.

clue.text: Shot material: "Take 1", it may be labelled

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the metal that shotgun pellets are made of
second meaning: to take someone somewhere, to guide them
third meaning: in this puzzle 1 is the theme word, and this is a chemical element

explanation.walkthrough: 'it may be labelled' is a link: the word could be the label for each of the three senses. In this puzzle a bare '1' points to the theme answer at 1-across, so it means a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal used for shotgun pellets, a verb for guiding someone, and a chemical element with symbol Pb.

clue.text: Is his work against the grain?

definitions.text: Is his work against the grain?

parts.words: Is his work against the grain?
parts.note: against the grain usually means contrary to nature; here it is literal, a man whose stones press against grain to grind it into flour

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'against the grain' means awkward or unnatural; read literally, it is someone grinding corn between millstones.
explanation.definitionFit: A miller's trade is grinding cereal into flour, so his daily labour is literally pressed against the grain.

clue.text: Raise flag to idol? Not quite there!

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something reads it upwards, so the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: rag is slang for a flag, especially a tattered one
an icon is an idol, an object of worship

explanation.surface: A disappointed cry from someone who hoisted a banner to a hero and missed the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' works on the whole of RAG + ICON, written upwards in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from fairground games where a near miss won no prize; it means close but not successful.

clue.text: Component of several items here, oddly shown in art forms

indicators.note: oddly means the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of these words are taken

parts.note: the source of the letters

explanation.surface: Something displayed in a gallery is made up of strange pieces of creative work.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'several items here' are the chemical elements that make up the theme answers; 'shown in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Every chemical element in the grid, such as gold or zinc, is built from these smallest particles of matter.

clue.text: Cover holidaymakers arranged when leaving Rio, led astray

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of holidaymakers are put into a new order
astray tells us the letters of led go missing too, wandered off from the mix

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tourists organised a trip but got lost after leaving the Brazilian city of Rio.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLIDAYMAKERS has six letters too many: 'when leaving' removes RIO and LED, and the remaining HAYMAKS rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a veil worn by some Muslim women in public, covering the face below the eyes.

clue.text: Entrée given the setter to Ascot?

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
to and at both mark place, as in 'going to/at the shops'
Ascot is an English racecourse, an example of a course

explanation.surface: A setter is invited to the races at Ascot, a smart event in the English social calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link. Ascot is a famous racecourse in Berkshire, England, where Royal Ascot is held.
explanation.definitionFit: In formal menus an entrée is the main dish, the substantial serving of meat between the starter and dessert.

clue.text: Large waves in mid-June touching fringes of Argyll; that's not normal

parts.note: the middle letters of June
seas are large waves, as in 'heavy seas'
on means touching, as a picture on a wall

indicators.note: fringes are the edges, so the first and last letters of Argyll

explanation.surface: Big waves on the Scottish coast of Argyll in midsummer would be unusual weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'that's' are links. Argyll is a region on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather that does not fit the time of year is abnormal for the season.

clue.text: 1 describes this knee joint regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter at even steps, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

parts.note: the source of the letters

explanation.surface: A medical description of the way a knee joint works.
explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle 1 is the theme word, so '1 describes this' means the answer is a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a noble gas, the chemical element used in glowing advertising signs.

clue.text: Delusive pianist beginning to compose promising notes

parts.note: Manuel de Falla, the Spanish composer, was also a concert pianist

indicators.note: beginning to compose means its first letter

parts.note: IOUs are notes promising to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A misleading tale of a pianist who starts writing music that shows promise.
explanation.walkthrough: Falla was a Spanish composer and pianist; an IOU (I owe you) is a written promise to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe reasoning or beliefs that are based on mistaken ideas and so deceive.

clue.text: Dash to drop son in right place for dance

indicators.note: to drop means the letter for right is taken out of the dash word
in shows the son letter goes in where the other came out
in right place means in the position of the right letter, a swap

parts.note: to hurtle is to dash, move fast
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A rushed instruction to a parent to leave the boy in the correct spot for a dance class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop son in right place' puts S where R stood in HURTLE. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The disco line dance of the 1970s, made famous by the Van McCoy record, shares its name with hurrying.

clue.text: 2 claiming Intellectual Property Rights? Watch my mouth!

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the rights letters go inside

parts.note: 2 is the answer at 2-down, the metal used for shot
IPR is the standard abbreviation for intellectual property rights

explanation.surface: A metal claims copyright protection and warns a rival to watch what they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 refers to the answer at 2-down, which holds IPR.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person may ask you to face them so they can read words from the movement of your lips.

clue.text: Hurry! The setter's attending court once Wally's gone, getting sanction

parts.note: leg it is slang for hurry, run away
the setter is, from his point of view, I'm

indicators.note: gone means the fool is removed from the old court

parts.note: an assize was a former English court of law
a wally is British slang for a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A rushed setter attends court and gets approval once a hapless fellow has left.
explanation.walkthrough: Assizes were periodic county courts in England, abolished in 1971; a wally is a British slang word for an idiot. 'attending' and 'getting' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something lawful or officially approved, to give it authority.

clue.text: Half the force embellishing removal of elder's crown?

definitions.note: the question mark flags that the elder is the tree, not an older person

parts.note: the force is the police; half of POLICE gives the first three letters
larding a speech means embellishing it with extra flourishes

explanation.surface: Half of a police force is busy decorating a ceremony in which an elder loses his crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The elder is a tree, and its crown is its top branches, not an elderly ruler losing office.
explanation.definitionFit: This forestry practice cuts back the upper branches of a tree such as elder to encourage dense new growth.

clue.text: She bowed beautifully and stood up reasonably content

indicators.note: content means contained, the letters held within these words

explanation.surface: A performer curtsied gracefully, then stood, reasonably pleased with her performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowed' looks like a curtsy, but it is the drawing of a bow across strings. Jacqueline du Pré was a celebrated English cellist.
explanation.definitionFit: The cellist Jacqueline du Pré was famous for her passionate bowing, especially in Elgar's Cello Concerto.

clue.text: Grave robber finally snapped by friend — carousing, without giving a damn about it

indicators.note: snapped by suggests being caught, so the letter is held within the friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of robber
without means the caring letters are taken away from carousing

parts.note: the word from which letters are removed
to give a damn about something is to care about it

explanation.surface: A grave robber is caught by a careless drinking companion on a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks part of 'grave robber', but it is the definition on its own. CARING comes out of CAROUSING in order, leaving OUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dangerously precarious situation is serious, so the archaic-sounding adjective means grave.

clue.text: Possibly G, F, or just P?

definitions.text: Possibly G, F, or just P?

parts.words: Possibly G, F, or just P?
parts.note: G suggests grand, F suggests forte, and P is the musical mark meaning softly; all three point to one keyboard instrument

explanation.walkthrough: The letters look like musical notes, but G stands for grand, F for forte, and P is the dynamic marking: all lead to the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is a kind of this instrument, its full name is pianoforte, and in scores p marks a soft passage.

clue.text: Problem with current King? He required so many twists and turns before succeeding!

definitions.text: He required so many twists and turns before succeeding!

parts.note: rub means a problem, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'
I is the symbol for electric current in physics
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: Someone frustrated by a puzzle involving electricity and a monarch, needing endless attempts before success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. The definition describes the inventor of the twisting cube puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernő Rubik, the Hungarian inventor, took a long time and many rotations to solve his own cube puzzle.

clue.text: Golf, perhaps, with a hole in 1? Yes, it is!

definitions.note: in this puzzle 1 is the theme word, so a chemical element is meant

parts.note: Golf is the radio alphabet word for G
something with a hole worn through it is old

explanation.surface: A golfer asks whether a hole in one counts as something special, and is told it does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Golf as one example of the radio alphabet; 'in' and 'Yes, it is!' are links confirming the element.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the precious metal with symbol Au, one of the chemical elements.

clue.text: 1 entity that's smooth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in this puzzle 1 is the theme word, so this is a chemical element
second meaning: to press creases out of fabric with a heated appliance

explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link. The bare number 1 points to the theme answer at 1-across.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal with symbol Fe, and the verb for pressing clothes flat with a hot appliance.

clue.text: Rip current at last switched in river

indicators.note: switched means the order is changed, so the last letter of current goes in front
at last means the final letter of current

parts.note: a rent is a rip, a tear in cloth

explanation.surface: A dangerous rip current finally changes course in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rip current' reads as one phrase but splits: Rip gives RENT, current gives its last letter, which 'switched' moves to the front. The Trent is a major English river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is one of England's longest rivers, flowing through the Midlands to the Humber.

clue.text: From that disturbed forefather, far away

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of forefather are thrown into disorder
away shows the letters of far are taken out of the mix

explanation.surface: An ancestor is upset at living such a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove F, A and R from FOREFATHER and rearrange OREFTHE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal legal word meaning of that or from that thing, as in 'and the proceeds thereof'.

clue.text: Information's included in application. That's a wrap!

indicators.note: included in means one piece is put inside another

parts.note: toil is hard work, application to a task
INF is an abbreviation for information

explanation.surface: Data is attached to a form, and the job is done: a film director's call at the end of shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's a wrap!' sounds like the film-set call; the definition is just 'a wrap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin metal sheeting is used to wrap food for cooking or storage.

clue.text: Section of large farm placed in trustee's hands

indicators.note: placed in means one piece is set inside another

parts.note: the hands are the extremities, the first and last letters of trustee
a ranch is a large farm, especially for cattle

explanation.surface: Part of a big agricultural estate is put under the care of a trustee.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or slice, especially a part of a larger sum of money.

clue.text: Apply lotion liberally? It's boring

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as a phrase, rub in oil thoroughly
second meaning: a drilled shaft, a bore, for extracting petroleum

explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling a hole in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into a verb and an adverb it means grease generously; as one word it is a shaft drilled to extract petroleum.

clue.text: See 1
See 1
"Such refreshment is 1 in church." Sounds like a complaint!

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is pronounced like the word for a complaint

parts.note: a whine is a complaint, a moan

explanation.surface: A churchgoer grumbles about the refreshments, and the complaint is noted.
explanation.walkthrough: At Communion the bread and the drink are called the elements, so this links to the theme answer at 1.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian Communion the consecrated bread and the drink from the chalice are known as the elements.

clue.text: It's 1 of four intrinsic "roots" Empedocles initially provided

definitions.text: It's 1 of four intrinsic "roots" Empedocles initially provided

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A statement about the ancient Greek philosopher Empedocles and his theory of four basic roots of matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Empedocles called the four classical elements 'roots'; the whole clue defines the answer and the first letters of four of its words spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth, air, water and the burning one were the four classical elements of Greek philosophy.

clue.text: Post held inside newspaper cunningly, to hide rips

indicators.note: cunningly means the letters are cleverly rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone working at a paper slyly conceals damage to the pages.
explanation.definitionFit: The top job at a newspaper is a position or post held by whoever directs its content.

clue.text: 1 substance has variable factor incorporated

definitions.note: in this puzzle 1 is the theme word, so a chemical element

parts.note: z is a conventional algebraic variable, a factor in an equation
Inc. is the abbreviation for incorporated, used after US company names

explanation.surface: A chemical substance turns out to contain some changeable ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link. In algebra x, y and z are the standard unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the bluish-white metal with symbol Zn, used for galvanising steel.

clue.text: One self-employed totter in France floundering

indicators.note: in places the totter word inside the jumbled country
floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: to reel is to totter, stagger

explanation.surface: A self-employed person staggers about in France, struggling to stay upright.
explanation.walkthrough: FRANCE rearranged becomes F ANCER, with REEL inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelancer works independently for different clients rather than as a salaried employee.
